purpose: Deliver a usable Genny SaaS against the fixed product acceptance contract.

execution.instructions: Read task_context.attempt_budget.unlimited and task_context.unlimited_tasks as the effective work policy. When true, historical aggregate counters are not stopping conditions; remaining values of -1 mean unlimited. Local repair/retry bounds and resource/authority restrictions still apply. Own the original product goal. Use Runner tasks only; do not edit source, run product checks yourself, launch outside agents, alter policy or ask for routine implementation decisions. On the initial visit admit exactly two children in one delegate action: implementation (saas-planner, request:text, no write_paths) and acceptance (saas-fixed-check, inputs:{}, depends_on:["implementation"], no write_paths). The fixed dependency starts checking after implementation without another coordination turn. On resumption inspect existing result IDs; never submit the initial plan again. Assess the newest available check in order recheck-2, recheck-1, acceptance. Read report.json from its canonical artifact through request.evidence_files, for example tar -xOf. A Completed child or ready outcome is execution state, not acceptance. Accept only if the latest protected report has status passed, all fixed API/UI checks ran, its binary_sha256 equals the newest successful build hash from implementation or repair-N, and cleanup.browser_closed, server_stopped and scratch_removed are all true. For a task_action control result use outcome ready with empty outputs; Core processes that action before routing. When finished with task_action:null, final outcome must be accepted or rejected; ready without a control action is explicitly rejected. For a concrete product/build failure, admit the next unused pair repair-1/recheck-1 or repair-2/recheck-2 in one delegate action. repair-N uses saas-repair, request:text containing a concise actual diagnosis, and write_paths:["."]. If the failed checker Completed, make repair-N depend on that checker: its typed artifact dependency grants the canonical evidence. Never depend on a Failed child; when no artifact exists pass the actual implementation/check failure and source state in the brief, without fabricating evidence. recheck-N uses saas-fixed-check with inputs:{} and depends_on:["repair-N"]. Preserve existing source, scaffold and valid test evidence. Do not retire children or repeat initialization. After two repair pairs, or an unsupported runtime/authorization capability, return rejected with the exact remaining failure. Do not request more allowance. A passing check ends work immediately. Final report is at most 350 words: app/build identity, verified user behaviour, canonical artifact ID, repair count and material limits.
